context: linear · tower by tower: foundations → erection → stringing; right-of-way and outages govern

brief.intro: New to this project type? An overhead transmission line carries high-voltage power (typically 66 kV to 500 kV) across country on steel lattice towers or poles. The work is a moving production line of three crews that follow each other along the route: foundations, tower erection, then stringing of the conductors and the earth wire. Nothing is technically difficult to repeat — the hard parts are getting onto the land (right-of-way, access tracks, crop and landowner compensation), the special places where the line crosses roads, railways, rivers or other power lines, and the final connection into live substations, which needs an outage granted by the grid operator on a fixed date.

scope.name: Route survey & tower spotting
scope.desc: Detailed survey and profile to fix each tower position, height and type.

scope.name: Right-of-way & access
scope.desc: Land access, clearance of the corridor and temporary access tracks to each tower.

scope.name: Soil investigation
scope.desc: A borehole or probe at tower locations to select the foundation type.

scope.name: Tower foundations
scope.desc: Pad-and-chimney, pile or rock-anchor foundations with stub setting.

scope.name: Tower earthing
scope.desc: Earthing of each tower and measurement of its resistance.

scope.name: Tower erection
scope.desc: Assembly and erection of suspension and tension (angle) towers.

scope.name: Insulators & hardware
scope.desc: Insulator strings and fittings hung on each tower.

scope.name: Conductor & earth-wire stringing
scope.desc: Tension stringing of conductors and OPGW, sagging and clamping, section by section.

scope.name: Crossings
scope.desc: Protected crossings of roads, railways, rivers and existing lines.

scope.name: Line accessories
scope.desc: Spacers, dampers, aircraft warning spheres, number and danger plates.

scope.name: Testing & energisation
scope.desc: Final inspection, line tests, connection to the substation gantries and energisation.

must_get_right: Right-of-way is the real critical path: a crew can only work where the land is released. Track ROW release tower by tower and keep the three crews in sequence behind it.
Plan foundations, erection and stringing as three production lines with a gap between them (concrete must gain strength before erection; whole sections must be erected before stringing).
Stringing needs a complete section between two tension towers — one missing tower stops kilometres of line.
Crossings of live lines, railways and highways, and the final connection to the substations, need permits and outages on fixed dates; put each one in the schedule as a milestone.

basis_of_planning.standard: AACE Recommended Practice 38R-06 — Documenting the Schedule Basis

sections.heading: Scheduling method & tools
sections.body: A Critical Path Method (CPM) network built in Primavera P6, developed to a Level 3 control schedule with retained-logic progress. Activities are organised by line section (between tension towers) and by crew — foundations, erection, stringing — so the number of towers founded, erected and strung can be read at any date.

sections.heading: Calendars & working time
sections.body: Standard site calendar for the three crews; reduced output is assumed in the wet season where access is across farmland. Outage works are on the dates granted by the grid operator.

sections.heading: Sequencing logic & critical path
sections.body: Per tower: ROW released → access → foundation → curing → erection. Per section: all towers erected → stringing → sagging → clamping. Then crossings, substation connections during outages, final inspection and energisation. The critical path follows the last section to be released by right-of-way, or the outage date.

sections.heading: Key assumptions
sections.body: Right-of-way is released at the planned rate and in route order; soil types are as investigated; outages are granted on the requested dates; the substations at both ends are ready to receive the line.

sections.heading: Access, resource & site constraints
sections.body: Access is seasonal across fields and wadis; crews and their plant must move along the route; live-line crossings and proximity to existing lines impose clearances and outage windows.

sections.heading: Risks, float & contingency
sections.body: Main risks: right-of-way and landowner disputes, unexpected ground (rock, high water table) changing foundation types, late tower steel after type tests, theft of materials, and refused or moved outages. Contingency is held before the energisation date.

sections.heading: Schedule levels of detail
sections.body: Reported at Level 1 (milestones) and Level 2 (summary) to the client; controlled at Level 3 by line section and crew; expanded to Level 4–5 lookahead for the foundation, erection and stringing gangs — consistent with AACE 37R-06.
